A.why: Pale plated suit with separate legs; no gown silhouette, hem band floats at ankles with a gap at the knee.
A.fix: Join thigh plates and hem into one closed flared tasset skirt from waist to shin; taper the banded shoulders.

B.why: Clear fitted-bodice gown with stepped flared skirt and crenellated crown, but heavy green cube sleeves broaden the shoulders.
B.fix: Slim the moss sleeve blocks and keep the shoulder line pale and narrow; carry pale stone onto the dark back skirt.

C.why: Solid tiered stone construction but a straight column skirt and dominant moss green read as robe or pillar.
C.fix: Flare the skirt tiers into an A or bell shape; reduce green to an accent and slim the shoulder blocks.

D.why: Most elegant aged-stone palette with a scalloped tasset skirt and V-necklace; wide pale sleeve slabs and a dark back hold it back.
D.fix: Narrow and taper the sleeves at the shoulder; pale stone on the back tassets; keep the flare in profile.

E.why: Clean but timid monochrome grey A-line; weak waist, flat helm and pauldron-like stepped sleeves; back reads as iron.
E.fix: Cinch the waist with a bronze girdle, add a crown or crest, slim the sleeves, and add moss and bronze accents.

F.why: Ziggurat skirt makes unmistakable concentric ruin rings from the ARPG camera; spired crown and palette on brief; stiff and blocky at the shoulder.
F.fix: Slim the green shoulder cubes; vary the tier heights for grace and cap the hollow bottom ring.

notes: F has the strongest top-down family read (stepped stone skirt). D is the most elegant and on-palette but too broad at the shoulder. B and F share the same heavy green-cube sleeve fault. All candidates leave the back dark grey or green, which weakens the read when the character faces away. A lacks a skirt entirely.
